subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw keep Docker `no-new-privileges` mandatory for sandbox containers, add an explicit dangerous opt-out, or limit this report to diagnostics/image compatibility work?
rationale: The user-visible failure is well supported, but every functional recovery path either weakens a Docker sandbox hardening flag or adds a new config/security surface, which repository policy treats as maintainer-owned direction.

options.title: Add audited opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named dangerous `sandbox.docker` opt-out with doctor/security reporting, and require real Docker proof on an affected host.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Leave the hardening mandatory and add doctor/status/session diagnostics that explain the host incompatibility and point users to supported host or runtime fixes.

options.title: Investigate image/runtime compatibility first
options.body: Hold config changes until maintainers prove whether the default sandbox image or host Docker/runc/AppArmor combination can be made compatible without weakening the flag.

recommendation.title: Add audited opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named dangerous `sandbox.docker` opt-out with doctor/security reporting, and require real Docker proof on an affected host.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on sandbox security/config policy, and the relevant history traces both the original sandbox feature and dangerous-override policy work to this owner path.
